clue.text: Exchange rate positive to provide wealth

indicators.note: to exchange is to swap things about, so the letters of the next word are switched around

parts.note: positive means certain, sure

explanation.surface: A favourable exchange rate makes someone rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange' rearranges RATE into TREA; add SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is a store of riches, so it stands for wealth.

clue.text: One holds the occupant to be safe

definitions.text: One holds the occupant to be safe

parts.words: One holds the occupant to be safe
parts.note: read as a description of a car safety device that straps a passenger into a seat

explanation.surface: Something keeps a person safe in place, perhaps a guard or a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's strap restrains the person sitting there for safety in a crash.

clue.text: Made off with axe and rifle

parts.note: made off means fled, ran
to axe someone is to fire them, sack

explanation.surface: A thief escaped carrying an axe and a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun noun; here it is the verb, to search through and plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search it roughly and steal from it, a synonym.

clue.text: eg Jane Eyre's tailless horse

indicators.note: tailless says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Jane Eyre is the title character and leading lady of Charlotte Bronte's novel, a heroine

explanation.surface: A question about the bobtailed horse belonging to a famous fictional governess.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. 'horse' looks like part of the picture but is the definition: horse is slang for the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is old street slang for the opiate drug.

clue.text: Commit to prison for parody say

definitions.meaning: to send someone up is to jail them, chiefly British and American slang
a mocking imitation is an example of a parody

explanation.definitionFit: Being jailed and a satirical skit share the same two-word phrase, one a verb, one a noun.

clue.text: In which people are up for seventy-two hours

definitions.text: In which people are up for seventy-two hours

parts.words: In which people are up for seventy-two hours
parts.note: being up suggests staying awake, but riders are up on horseback in an equestrian competition lasting that many days

explanation.surface: An all-night marathon where people stay awake for three days.
explanation.walkthrough: In horse riding, a rider is 'up' when mounted; the event combines dressage, cross-country and showjumping over successive days.
explanation.definitionFit: An equestrian contest held over three days keeps its riders mounted through that span.

clue.text: Spreading of ointment has produced Greek tragedy

indicators.note: spreading the words about like a cream on skin scatters their letters

explanation.surface: Smearing on some ointment led to a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spreading' rearranges OF OINTMENT HAS into the title of Shakespeare's play about a misanthrope of ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play about a generous Athenian turned misanthrope is a tragedy set in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Keep in the smoke

parts.note: a keep is a castle's main fortress, and the Smoke is a nickname for London, so this is the castle there

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay indoors where it is smoky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Smoke' (or 'the Big Smoke') is British slang for London. The White Tower is a famous keep.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortress on the Thames is a castle keep in Britain's capital, nicknamed the Smoke.

clue.text: One member with skill to pass on

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP, Member of Parliament
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A politician with talent wants to share it.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart knowledge is to pass it on to someone, a synonym.

clue.text: Disclose sad denouement

parts.note: to disclose is to reveal, show
feeling down means feeling sad

explanation.surface: A gloomy ending to a story is revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: A final decisive confrontation is the climax or resolution of a drama.

clue.text: Call from the Cotswolds?

parts.note: the Cotswolds are English hills famous for sheep farming, so the call is a bleat

explanation.surface: A phone call from a rural region of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cotswolds, a hilly area in southern England, grew rich on wool; the call is the animal's cry, not a telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep's bleat is the noise heard from a region known for its flocks.

clue.text: One knight certain to take cover

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N is the chess notation for knight
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A single knight confident about diving for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take cover' suggests hiding; here it means buying an insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking out a policy against loss gives financial protection, called cover.

clue.text: Study high church feature, using plot?

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
a tall tapering steeple tops many churches

explanation.surface: Someone examines a lofty church to hatch a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high church' looks like the Anglican tradition, but 'high' describes the tall structure.
explanation.definitionFit: To plot is to scheme secretly together, a synonym.

clue.text: Very little French money for son going to university

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
OU is the Open University, the UK's distance-learning institution

explanation.surface: A son heading off to college has hardly any cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' simply sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-value old French coin, hence a byword for almost no money.

clue.text: Accomplishes things

definitions.meaning: to effect a change is to bring it about
personal belongings, as in a dead person's possessions

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for bringing about and a noun for one's belongings.

clue.text: Better headgear

definitions.meaning: to outdo or top, as in capping a joke

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to outdo a rival and a brimmed hat.

clue.text: Slightly oiled frontal hair in outskirts of Surrey

indicators.note: in puts the hair piece inside the county's letters
outskirts are the edges, so the word's first and last letters are taken

parts.note: a quiff is a tuft of hair brushed up at the front

explanation.surface: A man with a slicked-back quiff in a Surrey suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oiled' suggests hair oil; here it is slang for drunk. Surrey is a county south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tipsy is a mild drunkenness, and oiled is slang for drunk.

clue.text: Dilemma when in France, over a railway

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the rest

parts.note: quand is French for when

explanation.surface: A predicament over a French railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is a state of perplexity over what to do, a synonym.

clue.text: Break in for travel plan

indicators.note: a plan arranges things, so the letters of travel are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A gap in a schedule set aside for a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plan' is used as a verb here: to plan is to lay things out, so the letters are set in a new order. 'Break' is a noun, a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a pause between parts, like a break at a theatre.

clue.text: Sideways, as a neck, injured

indicators.note: an injured thing is damaged and out of shape, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A person glances sideways because their neck is hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' scrambles only the last two words; the first word of the clue stays as written at the front of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to glance sideways, often in suspicion.

clue.text: Son meddles with post impressionists!

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to tamper with something is to meddle with it

explanation.surface: A son interfering with a Post-Impressionist painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post impressionists' suggests painters like Cezanne; here they are people or devices that print marks on mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Franking machines and clerks leave inked impressions on letters and parcels.

clue.text: Cricketer will perform in petulant mood?

indicators.note: in puts the performing word inside the sulky word

parts.note: a miff is a fit of pique
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: A cricketer will play in a sulk.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a fielding position in cricket, standing near the bowler on the off side; the player there stands for the position.
explanation.definitionFit: This fielder stands near the bowler on the off side, so names a cricketer.

clue.text: Property in eastern country

parts.note: a state is a country

explanation.surface: Someone owns real estate in an eastern land.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is landed property or a person's assets.

clue.text: A universal god and creator

parts.note: U is the British film rating for universal
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A god of everything who made the world.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is the originator of something, especially a writer.

clue.text: Stock of cordial, mainly

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: cordial means warm and friendly, kind

explanation.surface: A supply of fruit cordial, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like a store of drink; it means family line, and 'cordial' is the adjective, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock means lineage or family, and kin are relatives.

clue.text: At end, vet got into a feud

indicators.note: got into here suggests the words got into a tangle, so their letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: In the end, a vet became embroiled in a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a long bitter quarrel, a synonym.

clue.text: Scoff free in river

indicators.note: in puts the freeing word inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a free swim in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' could mean eat greedily; here it is to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to mock with contempt, a synonym.

clue.text: Her Majesty's fire screen?

parts.note: suggests a royal fireguard, but Her Majesty's is a London theatre, which has a fireproof barrier before the stage

explanation.surface: A screen guarding the Queen's fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: Her Majesty's Theatre is in London's West End; theatres must have a fireproof curtain that can drop between stage and audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's fireproof drop screen separates stage from audience in case of blaze.
